# Print

Writes a value's text to standard output.

```rux
pub func Print(value: String) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: StringView) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: char8[..]) -> IoError?
pub func Print(#Format() format: char8[..], ...) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: bool8) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: bool16) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: bool32) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: bool64) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: bool128) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: bool256) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: bool512) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: char8) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: char16) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: char32) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: int8) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: int16) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: int32) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: int64) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: uint8) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: uint16) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: uint32) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: uint64) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: int) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: uint) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: float8) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: float16) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: float32) -> IoError?
pub func Print(value: float64) -> IoError?
```

A `String`, a `StringView` or a `char8[..]` is written as the UTF-8 bytes it holds, unchanged: nothing is
substituted and no brace is special, so `Print("{{}}")` writes `{{}}`. Each primitive overload writes its value as
[`PrintValue`](/docs/api/io/print#print-value) does, through the type's `Display` conformance, and any other value goes through [`PrintValue`](/docs/api/io/print#print-value) itself.
Given arguments after it, the first text is a pattern instead: each `{}` or `{:spec}` takes the next argument in
order, and `{{` and `}}` write a literal brace.
Every overload returns the failure its write met as an [`IoError`](/docs/api/io/io-error), or `none`. A program logging to a terminal loses
nothing by ignoring it; one whose output feeds a pipe that may close has something to look at.

## Related

<h3 id="print-value"><code>PrintValue</code></h3>

```rux
pub func PrintValue(value: Display) -> IoError?
```

Writes a value's text to standard output.
Nothing is allocated: the value writes itself straight to the stream.
The value arrives as an interface value, which copies it — or takes it, for a type that prohibits copying.
[`WriteValueLine`](/docs/api/io/print-line#write-value-line) is the borrowing form, and takes any destination, so a value that must not be given up goes
through a [`ConsoleWriter`](/docs/api/io/console-writer) and that instead.
A stream failure is returned as the stream reported it. A formatting failure on a healthy stream is translated
by [`ToIoError`](/docs/api/io/io-error#to-io-error), so a request that was wrong arrives as `InvalidInput` and stays distinguishable from anything
the destination did. Which formatting failure it was does not survive that translation, since [`IoError`](/docs/api/io/io-error) has no
room for one; a caller who needs it builds a [`ConsoleWriter`](/docs/api/io/console-writer) and calls `Text::WriteValue` themselves.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Io/Src/Print.rux#L47)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type      | Description        |
| ------- | --------- | ------------------ |
| `value` | `Display` | the value to write |

**Returns**: what the stream reported, or the translated formatting failure on a healthy stream, or `none`
